attribution.note: Marcus wrote this himself as one of his own bullet points in his own essay.

semantics.note: Present-tense statement of the current state. It is offered as a reason for his bubble forecast, but the bullet itself is an observation. Reading it as generative AI is fair given the context.

contract.note: An informed reader would take 'plateau' to mean meaningful capability gains have stalled, so the plain reading is ordinary. The quarter is the evaluator's choice. Reading it as a slower pace of gains is a flagged alternative, but the statement is firm and the reading is not stretched.

evidence.note: Independent LMSYS arena, June 10–25, 2024: GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 score notably higher than GPT-4 Turbo and Gemini 1.5 Pro. These are preference votes, so stylistic effects may play a part.

Independent OlympicArena benchmark, June 2024: a clear gap separates the newer frontier models from the older ones on hard multidisciplinary problems. It also says overall performance is unsatisfactory, which speaks to reliability, not to a stall.
Anthropic's own internal coding evaluation: 64% versus 38% for Claude 3 Opus. This is a company disclosure, not an independent finding, but it agrees with e1 and e2.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading, two independent evaluations from inside April–June 2024 show meaningful gains for the newer releases (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) over their predecessors on the same evaluations. A company coding result points the same way. That contradicts a plateau in capability. Remaining errors do not amount to a plateau.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence. The Libin quote before it is separate and is not used.

semantics.note: The 'Marcus says' framing is awkward but the content is faithful. It keeps 'for the most part', the three components, and the hallucination and error clause.

contract.note: The ordinary reading is fair, and it rightly lets 'for the most part' cover exceptions such as Google DeepMind. Requiring an allocation breakdown for the investment part is strict but reasonable, since Marcus gave no measure.

evidence.note: Meta disclosure: Llama 3.1 405B was a scaled-up model said to be competitive with GPT-4-class models. Consistent with clustering, but it is the company's own claim and says nothing on investment share.
Meta technical report admits hallucinations remain a major challenge. This fits the error clause for one lab only. Posted three days after the period ends.
June internal Anthropic comparison with its own earlier model. It shows progress over time, not cross-company differences in July.
Meta research beyond plain LLM scaling. It shows alternatives existed but gives no investment amounts.

reviews.rationale: The packet partly fits the capability-clustering and hallucination parts, mostly through company disclosures. It contains no comparable industry-wide breakdown of resources between LLM scaling and other approaches. The investment component, which the contract requires, therefore cannot be settled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his own essay.

semantics.note: Unqualified present-tense observation about generative AI applications.

contract.note: Treating a killer app as an application with compelling value and sustained demand, professional ones included, is an ordinary reading. The undefined threshold and the evaluator-chosen quarter are flagged.

evidence.note: Independent Reuters Institute survey, March–April 2024: frequent ChatGPT use is rare. This questions mass demand but does not rule out a compelling professional application.

Microsoft discloses 1.8M paid GitHub Copilot subscribers and reported productivity gains for the quarter ending March 2024. This counts against the claim, but it is company-reported and from an earlier period.

reviews.rationale: Neither item establishes application-specific sustained demand plus practical value inside April–June 2024. The Copilot evidence is material against the claim but is self-reported and dated to the prior quarter. Low population-wide use does not show that no killer app existed.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence, stated as his belief.

semantics.note: 'I believe' carries no graded or low confidence. Paired with 'can never be solved', it is a firm impossibility claim with an open horizon. The explanatory 'given their inherent nature' is kept.

contract.note: The contract reads 'solved' as dependable general reliability, not perfection. It allows a broadly validated counterexample or an applicable impossibility result to settle the claim early. Fair to his words.

evidence.note: 2026 Princeton preprint: agent reliability shows only small gains over 24 months. That documents persistent failures, but a finite record cannot settle 'never', and the paper gives no impossibility proof.

reviews.rationale: This is a universal forecast with no deadline. The packet contains neither an applicable impossibility result nor a broadly validated demonstration that reliability has been solved, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Continuing failures do not settle 'never'.
